elements.name: astar.delete_map
elements.description: Delete a map by its ID. This will free the memory used by the map.

parameters.name: map_id
parameters.doc: ID of the map to delete. Has to be an integer from 0 to 2^16 - 1.

elements.name: astar.setup
elements.description: Initial setup. You have to setup the astar before calling any other methods.

parameters.name: map_width
parameters.doc: Width of your map. This is generally width of your tilemap.

parameters.name: map_height
parameters.doc: Height of your map. This is generally width of your tilemap.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.doc:
Movement direction (astar.DIRECTION_FOUR or astar.DIRECTION_EIGHT)
`astar.DIRECTION_FOUR` - on a square grid that allows 4 directions of movement using Manhattan distance.
`astar.DIRECTION_EIGHT` - on a square grid that allows 8 directions of movement using Euclidean distance.

parameters.name: allocate
parameters.doc:
How many states should be internally allocated at a time. This can be hard to get correct. The higher the value, the more memory Patfinder will use.
- If you have a small map (a few thousand states?) it may make sense to pass in the maximum value. This will cache everything, and MicroPather will only need one main memory allocation. For a chess board, allocate  would be set to 8x8 (64)
- If your map is large, something like 1/4 the number of possible states is good.
- If your state space is huge, use a multiple (5-10x) of the normal path. "Occasionally" call `astar.reset_cache()` to free unused memory.

parameters.name: typical_adjacent
parameters.doc: Used to determine cache size. The typical number of adjacent states to a given state. (On a chessboard, 8.) Higher values use a little more memory.

parameters.name: cache[optional]
parameters.doc: Turn on path caching. Uses more memory (yet again) but at a huge speed advantage if you may call the pather with the same path or sub-path, which is common for pathing over maps in games.  Default is `true`

parameters.name: use_zero[optional]
parameters.doc: Toggle start index 0 or 1 for tables and tile positions. Also you can set it by call `astar.use_zero()`.  Default is `false`

parameters.name: map_vflip[optional]
parameters.doc: Flips the map vertically. This doesn't flip the coordinates. Also you can set it by call `astar.map_vflip()`. Default is `false`

parameters.name: map_id[optional]
parameters.doc: ID of the map. Has to be an integer from 0 to 2^16 - 1. Default is `0`.

elements.examples:
local map_width = 5
local map_height = 4
local direction = astar.DIRECTION_EIGHT
local allocate = map_width * map_height
local typical_adjacent = 8
local cache = true     -- Optional. Default is true
local flip_map = false -- Optional. Default is false

astar.setup("my_map", map_width, map_height, direction, allocate, typical_adjacent, cache, flip_map)

elements.name: astar.use_zero
elements.brief:
Toggle start index 0 or 1 for tables and tile positions.
If set to `false`, [astar.solve](#astarsolvestart_x-start_y-end_x-end_y), [astar.solve_near](#astarsolve_nearstart_x-start_y-max_cost), [astar.get_at](#astarget_atx-y), [astar.set_at](#astarset_atx-y-value) methods expect positions start with 1 and returns table indexes from **1**.
Default is `false` = 1

elements.name: astar.set_map
elements.description:
Set your map data.
* Setting new map data reset the current cache.

parameters.name: world
parameters.doc: Your tilemap data. Keep it simple as much as you can.

parameters.name: map_id[optional]
parameters.doc: ID of the map. Has to be an integer from 0 to 2^16 - 1. Default is `0`.

elements.name: astar.set_costs
elements.description:
Set costs for walkable tiles on your `world` table. This table keys determine the walkable area.
Table's sum must be the `astar.DIRECTION_FOUR` or `astar.DIRECTION_EIGHT`.

parameters.name: costs
parameters.doc: Table of costs for directions.

parameters.name: map_id[optional]
parameters.doc: ID of the map. Has to be an integer from 0 to 2^16 - 1. Default is `0`.

parameters.name: start_x
parameters.doc: Start tile X.

parameters.name: start_y
parameters.doc: Start tile Y.

parameters.name: end_x
parameters.doc: End tile X.

parameters.name: end_y
parameters.doc: End tile Y.

parameters.name: map_id[optional]
parameters.doc: ID of the map. Has to be an integer from 0 to 2^16 - 1. Default is `0`.

returnvalues.name: path
returnvalues.doc: Table with x and y coordinates. First value is the given start point.
